seoTitle: Replace Shopify's Add to Cart Button With an Affiliate Link
metaDescription: Swap Shopify's Add to Cart or Buy Now button for a link to an external affiliate page using a Custom Liquid block. No theme file surgery, and fully reversible.
intro:
An affiliate storefront has one awkward problem. Shopify is built to take the sale, and every product page ends in an Add to cart button that leads to your own checkout. You want that button to send the shopper to Amazon, a supplier, or whichever marketplace pays you the commission.

The clean way to do it is not hacking product-form.liquid. It's adding a Custom Liquid block in the theme editor that renders your own link styled as a button, then hiding the native buy buttons. This guide walks that method end to end, including the small CSS that makes the new button sit flush and full-width like the theme's own, and finishes with the link attributes and disclosure details that keep the setup professional instead of sketchy.

steps.heading: Pick the block approach over editing theme files
steps.body:
There are two ways to change what a product page's button does. You can open Edit code and rewrite the buy-buttons snippet, or add a Custom Liquid block through the theme editor's own interface. The block approach wins for an affiliate store: it survives theme updates, it's undone by deleting one block instead of hunting for what you changed, and it never risks breaking the product form for the rest of the site.

It also lets you keep the native buy buttons hidden instead of deleted, so switching a product back to real Shopify checkout later is a single toggle. Everything below uses that approach, and none of it touches a .liquid file directly.

steps.heading: Open your theme editor
steps.body: From the Shopify admin, go to Online Store, then Themes. Your live theme is the one marked Current theme (Dawn in the store shown here), with an Edit theme button on its row; Shopify's own documentation now uses that label, though some older recordings and guides still show it as Customize. Before you click it, take the thirty seconds to duplicate the theme from the three-dot menu beside it. You're about to change how every product page converts, and a duplicate is the difference between an instant rollback and rebuilding from memory. Then open the editor on the live copy.

image.caption: Online Store, Themes: Dawn set as the current theme, with the theme editor button on the right.

steps.heading: Find the Buy buttons block on the product template
steps.body:
In the theme editor, switch the Home page drop-down at the top to Products, then Default product, so you're editing an actual product layout. The Sections sidebar then shows the template's sections, and under Product information you get the individual blocks that make up the right-hand column: Text, Title, Price, Variant picker, Quantity selector, Buy buttons, Description and Share.

Buy buttons is the one that renders Add to cart and, when it's switched on, the Buy now button beneath it. Click through them once so you understand the stacking order. The block you're about to add will sit wherever you drop it in this list, and you want your affiliate button in the same position the customer's eye already expects.

image.caption: The Default product template with Product information expanded, showing Buy buttons among the blocks in the left panel.

steps.heading: Add a Custom Liquid block with your affiliate link
steps.body: At the bottom of the Product information block list, click Add block and choose Custom Liquid. A Liquid code box opens in the left panel, and whatever you put there renders exactly where the block sits. Paste an anchor tag pointing at your affiliate URL and give it the theme's own button class so it inherits the store's styling: Make An Enquiry. Swap the label for something that matches the destination, like Buy on Amazon or View on supplier site. The extra custom_url class does nothing on its own; it's there purely as a hook for the CSS in the next step. Drag the new block directly above or below Buy buttons so it lands where shoppers already look for the call to action.

image.caption: A Custom Liquid block holding the anchor tag and its style rules, with the resulting Make An Enquiry button rendered under Add to cart in the preview.

steps.heading: Style it to match the theme's own button
steps.body:
Out of the box the anchor renders as a shrink-to-fit link, not a full-width button, which looks obviously bolted on. Add a small style block underneath the anchor in the same Custom Liquid box to fix the width and spacing. The version in use here sets .custom_url to display: flex, width: 100% and margin: 0 with !important, then zeroes the margin on .product-form so the new button sits tight against the block above instead of leaving a gap where the old one used to breathe.

The !important flags are doing real work: theme button styles are specific, and without them your rules lose. Watch the live preview as you type; it re-renders on each change so you can see immediately whether the button spans the column properly.

steps.heading: Hide the native Add to cart and Buy now buttons
steps.body:
With your link in place, the page shows two calls to action, which is worse than either one alone. Hover the Buy buttons block in the left panel and click the eye icon to hide it. That's Shopify's own documented method, and it removes Add to cart and Buy now from the storefront without deleting the block, so you can bring them back with the same click.

If you want the affiliate redirect on only some products instead of all of them, don't hide the block on the default template. Create a separate product template instead (Products, then the ⊕ Create template option), hide Buy buttons on that copy, and assign it per product from the Theme template section on each product's admin page. Shopify's bulk editor can set the template column across many products at once if you're switching more than a handful.

steps.heading: Test the redirect and tidy up the details
steps.body:
Click Save, open a product page on the live storefront, and click the new button. It should leave your store and land on the affiliate product page with your tracking parameters intact. Test on mobile too, since the product column stacks differently and a button with a forced width can overflow.

Two additions are worth making while you're in the code box: target="_blank" so the shopper keeps your tab open, and rel="nofollow sponsored noopener" on the anchor, which is what search engines expect on paid links and closes a small security gap that comes with _blank. Finally, add a short affiliate disclosure near the button or in the footer. Most affiliate programmes require it, and it costs nothing in conversion when the button itself is honest about where it leads.

troubleshooting.problem: Both the affiliate button and Add to cart show on the page
troubleshooting.cause: The Buy buttons block is still visible on the template, sitting alongside the new Custom Liquid block.
troubleshooting.fix: Hover the Buy buttons block in the Sections sidebar and click the eye icon to hide it.

troubleshooting.problem: The new button is a small link, not a full-width button
troubleshooting.cause: An anchor tag has no width by default and the theme's button CSS is more specific than an unstyled class.
troubleshooting.fix: Add a style block in the same Custom Liquid box setting the class to display: flex, width: 100% with !important, so it overrides the theme's own rules.

troubleshooting.problem: The redirect applies to every product when only some should change
troubleshooting.cause: The changes were made directly on the Default product template, which every product uses unless told otherwise.
troubleshooting.fix: Create a separate product template, hide Buy buttons only there, and assign it to specific products from the Theme template section (or via bulk edit for many products).

faq.question: Do I have to edit theme code to redirect the Add to Cart button?
faq.answer: No. A Custom Liquid block added through the theme editor does the job. You paste an anchor tag pointing at your affiliate URL, style it, and hide the native Buy buttons block. Nothing in the theme's .liquid files changes.

faq.question: How do I hide the original Add to cart and Buy now buttons?
faq.answer: In the theme editor, hover the Buy buttons block under Product information and click the eye icon to hide it. That's Shopify's documented method, and it's reversible with the same click.

faq.question: Can I apply this to only some products?
faq.answer: Yes. Create a separate product template, hide Buy buttons on that copy, then assign it to specific products from the Theme template section on each product's admin page, or in bulk from the product list. Products left on the default template keep normal checkout.

faq.question: Why does my new button look small or misaligned?
faq.answer: An anchor tag doesn't fill the column by default. Set the link's class to display: flex and width: 100% with !important in a style block inside the same Custom Liquid box, and zero the surrounding product-form margin so the spacing matches the rest of the page.

faq.question: Should affiliate buttons use nofollow?
faq.answer: Yes. Add rel="nofollow sponsored noopener" to the anchor. Sponsored marks it as a paid link for search engines, and noopener closes the security gap that comes with opening links in a new tab.

faq.question: Is this reversible?
faq.answer: Completely. Delete the Custom Liquid block and unhide the Buy buttons block, and the page returns to standard Shopify checkout. Duplicating the theme before you start makes the rollback even safer.
